column2: the `/review` sole-finder slot split is underspecified versus the credit-sharing split. the plan says to compute `reviewer_slots` from proposer attribution but does not pin the split contract. `split_classification_attribution(..., column="reviewer_slots")` splits on `|`, while restored proposers are comma-separated (`codex-arch, cursor-testing`). mis-splitting treats co-proposed strings as one slot and can award a sole-finder bonus on shared findings or attach it to a non-scoreboard key.

`/review` bonus timing is ambiguous; `score_rows` cannot recover sole-finder per finding afterward. `score_rows` tuples omit finding id and co-proposed accepted findings emit multiple rows. a final stats pass over `score_rows` cannot tell which accepted rows were sole-finder versus shared, so bonus logic added only at aggregation time will be wrong or require fragile heuristics.

the active-bonus test plan omits a scope-drift case even though failure modes call out ordering before `_scope_drift()`. an accepted sole-finder `finding_n` rerouted to `kind=oos` by `_scope_drift()` could still receive `larch_unique_finder_bonus` if bonus gating keys only on `result==accepted` or runs before `is_oos` is set.

the plan says to update `_scoreboard()` for a bonus component but co-proposed findings already emit one `score_row` per reviewer. implementing sole-finder detection inside `_scoreboard()` per row would always see one reviewer and could award the bonus to every co-proposer on the same finding.
